name.text: Using Trig ratios to Find the Base

questiontext.text:
Solve for \(x\). Do not convert your answer to decimal form. Rationalize and simplify if needed.

Hint: To type trig expressions in your work:

  • Use sin (x ), cos(x) , tan (x) for sine, cosine, and tangent. Example: sin (30) → \(\sin 30 \)

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-2, 12, 12, -2], axis: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); /* Right-angle triangle coordinates */ const A = board.create('point', [0, 0], {name: '', fixed: true, size: 2}); // right angle const B = board.create('point', [10, 0], {name: '', fixed: true, size: 2}); // bottom right (angle theta) const C = board.create('point', [0, 10], {name: '', fixed: true, size: 2}); // top /* Triangle edges */ board.create('segment', [A, B]); board.create('segment', [A, C]); board.create('segment', [B, C]); /* Right-angle square at A */ board.create('polygon', [ board.create('point', [0, 0], {visible:false}), board.create('point', [1, 0], {visible:false}), board.create('point', [1, 1], {visible:false}), board.create('point', [0, 1], {visible:false}) ], { fillColor: 'white', fillOpacity: 1, borders: {strokeColor: 'black'} }); /* Labels */ board.create('text', [5, -0.5, 'x'], {fontSize: 14}); // base (horizontal) board.create('text', [5, 6, '{#hyp#}'], {fontSize: 14}); // hypotenuse board.create('text', [8, 0.5, '{#theta#}°'], {fontSize: 14}); // angle at B [[/jsxgraph]]

We have a right-angled triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left, hypotenuse {@hyp@}, and an angle {@theta@}° at the bottom-right. We need to find the base (horizontal side) x.

The base adjacent to the angle is related to the hypotenuse by the cosine ratio:

\[ \cos({@theta@}°) = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{x}{@hyp@} \]

Solving for x gives:

\[ x = {@hyp@} \,\cos({@theta@}°) \]

Evaluate exactly (no decimals):

  • \(\cos 30° = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)
  • \(\cos 45° = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\)
  • \(\cos 60° = \frac{1}{2}\)
  • For other angles (e.g. 35°, 40°, 55°), leave the answer as: \[ x = {@hyp@} \,\cos({@theta@}°) \] Replace \(\cos({@theta@}°)\) with a known exact value if possible.

Tips:

  • Write answers like \(\frac{{@hyp@}\sqrt{n}}{2}\), not with a root in the denominator.
  • Keep answers exact; do not convert to decimals.
